title: Incolor SSR Review: 600 Miles Later

takeaways.text: Slow to get up to speed but holds speed very well once there; the owner credits the 34 mm head tube, narrow seat mast and deep wheels.
The front end feels heavy out of the saddle, which he blames on the integrated bar and stem; few aftermarket bars fit and the spacers under the stem had to be 3D-printed for a neat look.

Unlike some reviewers, he found it very comfortable over a couple of months of daily riding, crediting the seat mast's compliance and his steel-spoked wheels; the bottom bracket feels extremely stiff.
His 58 cm disc build weighs about 17 lb (7.7 kg), the same as his rim-brake Tarmac SL6 build.
Because the integrated seat mast is cut to one height, he recommends it only for riders who already know their fit.

disclosure: Owner review of the presenter's own 58 cm SSR build; no sponsorship or supplied-product relationship is stated in the video.
summary: Owner ride review of a 58 cm Incolor SSR after about 600 miles, compared with the owner's rim-brake Tarmac SL6.
